newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police report threat to kill minister.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police report threat to kill minister.

text.p: Sri Lankan police said Thursday they had detained a suspected separatist Tamil rebel after a warning of a plot to kill Justice Minister G.L. Peiris.

Peiris cancelled plans to attend an insurance salesmen's meeting on Wednesday at a Colombo hotel after police were informed one of the salesmen present could be a suicide bomber from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) group.
Police took the man into custody, but found no evidence linking him to the LTTE, a group fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.

"At the moment he is a genuine insurance salesman from Jaffna (the rebels' former northern stronghold). But we're conducting further investigations," Colombo police chief D.M. Dissanayake told Reuters.
The man was still in custody on Thursday.
Peiris is believed to be the architect of a controversial peace plan proposed by the government to end a 13-year war with the LTTE, which the government says has killed more than 50,000 people.
The rebels are known to use suicide bombers to assassinate key government figures. A suspected LTTE suicide bomber killed Sri Lanka's president Ranasinghe Premadasa in 1993.

On Wednesday, a clash between the rebels and army commandoes in Kokkutuduwai north of the eastern port of Trincomalee, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of Colombo, left one soldier and seven rebels dead, military officials said.
